root_cause.text: The work handler processes multiple pending events from a per-connection `work_list` in a single workqueue execution, releasing each `iwcm_work` structure (which embeds the `work_struct`) back to a free list before the workqueue has finished with the corresponding `work_struct`, allowing that same `work_struct` to be re-initialized and re-queued while still considered pending by the workqueue, leading to internal list corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that "a single run of the work handler could process item N+1 and release it back to the free list while the actual workqueue entry is still queued. It could then get reused (INIT_WORK...) and lead to list corruption in the workqueue logic." The fix removes the `work_list` and processes events individually per workqueue item, avoiding the unsafe reuse pattern.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clean up the iwcm_work structure by removing the unused 'list' field.
intent_record.what: Removed the 'list' field from the 'iwcm_work' structure, which was a struct list_head member.
intent_record.how: The change reduces the memory footprint of each 'iwcm_work' instance by eliminating an unused linked list node. It does not alter any runtime behavior because the field was not referenced elsewhere in the codebase.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect initialization of work list node by removing INIT_LIST_HEAD to avoid list corruption.
intent_record.what: Removed the line 'INIT_LIST_HEAD(&work->list);' from alloc_work_entries function.
intent_record.how: The work structure's list member is no longer initialized as a standalone list head. Since the work structure is allocated with kzalloc, the pointers are zeroed. This change prevents the list node from being treated as a list head, which previously could cause corruption when the work is added to a real list.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove a BUG_ON that could cause a kernel panic when freeing a cm_id with a non-empty work_list, allowing graceful cleanup instead.
intent_record.what: Removed the BUG_ON assertion that checked if the work_list is empty before freeing the cm_id in iwcm_deref_id.
intent_record.how: Previously, if the reference count reached zero but the work_list was not empty, the kernel would panic. After removal, the code proceeds to free_cm_id regardless of the work_list state, avoiding a crash.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant initialization of work_list in iw_create_cm_id because the field is either unused or initialized elsewhere.
intent_record.what: Removed the line that initializes the work_list list head in the iw_cm_id_priv structure.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the work_list member will no longer be explicitly initialized to an empty list via INIT_LIST_HEAD. This may have no effect if the list is unused or is initialized elsewhere, or could cause issues if used without prior initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update comment for clarity and accuracy.
intent_record.what: The comment block before cm_work_handler was reworded: the first sentence changed from 'Process events on the work_list for the cm_id.' to 'Process events for the cm_id.' and the subsequent sentences were slightly rephrased for clarity.
intent_record.how: No change in runtime behavior; only the comment text is modified.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify event processing in cm_work_handler by removing batching, processing only one event per work invocation.
intent_record.what: Removed the while loop that processed all pending events from work_list in cm_work_handler; now only the triggering work item is processed. Removed associated spin_unlock/lock and list operations. Updated comment to remove description of event batching.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the work handler no longer drains multiple events from the work_list; each invocation processes exactly one event (the one that scheduled the work). Event processing is no longer batched, changing concurrency and ordering characteristics.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential list corruption or use-after-free by not adding work items to the cm_id_priv work_list, as the workqueue already provides proper lifecycle management.
intent_record.what: Removed the line `list_add_tail(&work->list, &cm_id_priv->work_list);` from the `cm_event_handler` function.
intent_record.how: The work item is no longer inserted into the `work_list` of `cm_id_priv`, but it is still queued to the workqueue via `queue_work`. Any subsequent enumeration of the `work_list` will not include this work item, which may affect flushing or cancellation logic.

bic_trace_step.reason: In cm_work_handler(), after copying the work struct into a local variable (lwork = *work), put_work(work) is called which returns the work to the free list. Immediately after, process_event() is called with &work->event, accessing the work struct after it has been freed to the list. Since the work struct is now available for reuse, cm_event_handler() can reinitialize and requeue the same work_struct via INIT_WORK and queue_work, causing a use-after-free and workqueue list corruption. No fix is present.

For each work item, it calls put_work(work) to return the iwcm_work structure to the free list (line ~318 in the diff: 'put_work(work);') before it has finished using the work->event in the subsequent call to process_event (line ~320: 'ret = process_event(cm_id_priv, &work->event);'). This releases the work structure back to the free list while the workqueue handler still holds a reference to it, allowing the same work_struct to be re-initialized and re-queued while still considered pending, leading to list corruption.
